newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crudes dip, pending tenders keep interest low.
newsitem.headline: Asia crudes dip, pending tenders keep interest low.

text.p: Trading on the Middle East crude market was thin on Thursday, as traders waited for the outcome of the Indian and Bangchak July purchase tenders.
India was heard to have attracted seven cargoes of Dubai, and several VLCCs of Qua Iboe crudes, traders said.
In the Bangchak tender, a refinery source said eight Oman cargoes were offered, as well as some Iranian, Arabian and Abu Dhabi crudes.
There were persistent talk a July Oman traded to a Chinese oil company at MPM -10 cents per barrel. But this was denied by the Chinese company.
Another shosha was heard to have sold June Duri to an Indonesian affiliate, but the deal could not be confirmed.
Indonesia's exports of Duri crude for June were smaller than had been expected and forced its affiliates to buy on the spot market to cover their commitments.
On the light Asian crudes, a producer sold a Tapis cargo loading June 20-25, to a shosha at APPI +45.
Destination of the cargo was uncertain, thought by traders to be either to Bangchak or to China.
It said it was looking to cover its July requirements, but had not concluded any trade yet.
The light Middle East crudes remained under pressure.
Bids for Qatar Marine were coming from QGPC -60, with Murban bid at ADNOC -40, traders said.
A second July trade for Vietnamese Bach Ho was sold by a shosha on Tuesday, at Minas APPI +45, reflecting improved demand for heavy sweet crudes.
A July Bach Ho heard done at Minas APPI +40 last week had surprised the market, as the premium was higher than had been expected at the time.
